deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft (Konzept) of Riemann's Inauguraldissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The page covers the end of Art. 8 and the start of Art. 9 (here headed '§. 9.'). The previous article (Art. 7 in the print) proved the divergence/Green theorem in the form ∫∫_T (∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y) dT = −∫_∂T (X cos ξ + Y cos η) ds. Here ξ and η are the angles that the inward normal makes with the x- and y-axes.

(1) Boundary coordinates. Measure arc length s along the boundary from a fixed starting point. Measure the distance p along the normal erected at the boundary point O_0, counted positive towards the interior. Near the boundary, x and y are then functions of (s,p). On the boundary:
- ∂x/∂p = cos ξ and ∂y/∂p = cos η, since (∂x/∂p, ∂y/∂p) is the inward unit normal n.
- ∂x/∂s = ±cos η and ∂y/∂s = ∓cos ξ, since the unit tangent is n rotated by ∓90°.

The upper signs hold when the direction of increasing s makes the same angle with the p-direction as the x-axis makes with the y-axis. In other words, rotating the s-direction by +90° gives the inward normal, so the interior lies to the left.

(2) Orientation convention. Riemann fixes the upper signs throughout. Hence ∂x/∂s = ∂y/∂p and ∂y/∂s = −∂x/∂p. These are formally Cauchy–Riemann-type relations between the (s,p) and (x,y) frames. He remarks that this choice does not essentially restrict generality.

(3) Interior lines. The same (s,p) apparatus is extended to curves inside T. An extra rule is needed to fix the signs of dp and ds, since their mutual relation is already fixed by (2):
- For a closed curve, one states which of the two regions it separates it is to bound; this fixes the sign of dp.
- For an open curve, one names its initial endpoint, where s is smallest; this fixes the sign of ds.

(4) Substituting cos ξ = ∂x/∂p = −∂y/∂s and cos η = ∂y/∂p = ∂x/∂s into Art. 7 gives:
∫∫_T (X_x + Y_y) dT = −∫_∂T (X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds = ∫_∂T (X ∂y/∂s − Y ∂x/∂s) ds.
The last form is the familiar ∮ (X dy − Y dx).

(5) Art. 9, Theorem I. Suppose X and Y are continuous (and, per the pencil note, finite) at all points of T and satisfy X_x + Y_y = 0. Then ∫_∂T (X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds = 0. This follows at once from (4).

The page then begins the additivity argument. Cut an arbitrary surface T_1 spread over the plane A into two pieces T_2 and T_3. The integral over ∂T_1 equals the sum of the integrals over ∂T_2 and ∂T_3, because the common cut is traversed with opposite inward normals and cancels. This is the lead-in to Riemann's Theorem II: the integral is unchanged under deformation of the boundary across regions where the hypotheses hold. The page breaks off mid-sentence.
errors: No mathematical errors. With p measured inward and the upper-sign convention (interior on the left), cos ξ = −dy/ds and cos η = dx/ds. Both the sign of the boundary integral and the equality of its two forms check out.
Minor: the transcription's '[?]' on the area element of the first integral. The ink may read like 'ds' but must mean dT (the area element); this is a slip of the pen or a misreading.

results.what: Boundary normal/tangent coordinates (s,p) with ∂x/∂s = ∂y/∂p, ∂y/∂s = −∂x/∂p under positive orientation
results.modern_name: Frenet-type boundary frame; positive (counterclockwise) orientation of the boundary

results.what: ∫∫(X_x+Y_y)dT = −∫(X x_p + Y y_p) ds = ∫(X y_s − Y x_s) ds
results.modern_name: Green's theorem / divergence theorem in the plane
results.usually_credited_to: Green 1828, Gauss, Ostrogradsky; this formulation appears in Riemann's 1851 dissertation Art. 7–8

results.what: If X_x+Y_y=0 in T, the boundary flux integral vanishes; additivity under cutting T into pieces
results.modern_name: Vanishing flux of a divergence-free field; precursor to the Cauchy integral theorem (Riemann's Art. 9 Theorem I/II)
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy (integral theorem, 1825); Riemann dissertation 1851 for this formulation

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation (Art. 8–9), nearly verbatim. The only novelty is drafting variants such as marginal rewordings and the 'stetig und endlich' hesitation.

transcription_corrections: In the first integral of the displayed equation the area element should be dT (surface element), not ds. The ink is ambiguous ('d5'-like), but the mathematics requires dT.
'nach innen' is written above a struck-out word; the struck word is illegible.
Section heading '§. 9.' corresponds to Art. 9 of the printed dissertation; 'II 6' at top right is a sheet/bundle numbering.
